items.followUp: Define Percentage-Mass/Volume and write its formula.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantities used in the percentage.
rubric.description: State that the percentage compares the volume of solute with the volume of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying both volumes.

rubric.why: Shows how the volume ratio is expressed as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

modelAnswer: Percentage-Volume/Volume is the volume of solute dissolved in 100 volumes of solution.
Percentage (v/v) = (volume of solute ÷ volume of solution) × 100.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of a true solution.

rubric.why: A suspension has particles that are not uniformly dispersed and may settle.
rubric.description: Give one characteristic concerning the heterogeneous nature or settling of suspension particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid characteristic.

rubric.why: These are other distinguishing properties of suspensions.
rubric.description: Give a second valid characteristic of a suspension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different valid characteristic.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture with particles large enough to be seen.
Its particles settle on standing and can be separated by filtration.

items.followUp: Why does a test tube become cold when an endothermic salt dissolves in water?

rubric.why: The observed warming is due to heat released during dissolution.
rubric.description: Identify dissolution of Li₂SO₄ as an exothermic process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that heat is released.

rubric.why: The heat of hydration released is greater than the energy absorbed in separating the ionic lattice.
rubric.description: Explain the energy balance that produces the warming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly comparing hydration and lattice energies.

modelAnswer: Dissolving Li₂SO₄ in water is exothermic, so heat is released and the test tube becomes warm.
The energy released during hydration of the ions is greater than the energy absorbed to separate the ions in the lattice.

items.followUp: Name any two metals that are less reactive than sodium.

rubric.why: The question asks for an example of a very reactive metal.
rubric.description: Give one suitable example of a very reactive metal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

rubric.description: Give a second suitable example of a very reactive metal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different correct example.

modelAnswer: Sodium (Na) and potassium (K) are two very reactive metals.

items.followUp: Why is the atomic radius of potassium greater than that of sodium?

rubric.why: Sodium’s valence electron is closer to the nucleus than potassium’s.
rubric.description: Compare the atomic size or shell structure of Na and K.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Na has a smaller radius or fewer occupied shells.

rubric.why: The stronger attraction makes it harder to remove sodium’s outer electron.
rubric.description: Relate the comparison to the energy needed to remove the outer electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting stronger attraction or less shielding in Na to its higher ionization energy.

modelAnswer: Na has a smaller atomic radius and fewer occupied electron shells than K.
Therefore, Na’s outer electron is closer to the nucleus and experiences stronger attraction, so more energy is needed to remove it.

items.followUp: Write balanced chemical equations for the reactions of hydrogen with oxygen and bromine.

rubric.why: This is the balanced reaction of hydrogen with fluorine.
rubric.description: Write the balanced equation for H₂ reacting with F₂.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct balanced equation.

rubric.why: This is the balanced reaction of hydrogen with chlorine.
rubric.description: Write the balanced equation for H₂ reacting with Cl₂.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct balanced equation.

modelAnswer: H₂ + F₂ → 2HF
H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl

items.followUp: Write any five characteristics of an electron beam (cathode rays).

rubric.why: These are two fundamental properties of cathode rays.
rubric.description: State that cathode rays travel in straight lines and carry negative charge.

rubric.why: Cathode rays respond to fields as negatively charged particles and produce fluorescence.
rubric.description: Describe deflection towards the positive plate and production of fluorescence.

rubric.why: Any one additional valid property completes the five requested characteristics.
rubric.description: Give a further characteristic, such as casting shadows or possessing mass and kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid additional property.

modelAnswer: Cathode rays travel in straight lines.
They carry a negative charge.
They are deflected by an electric field towards the positive plate.
They produce fluorescence when they strike certain materials.
They cast shadows when an object is placed in their path.

items.followUp: Define an element, a compound, a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: An atom is the smallest unit of an element involved in chemical change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of an atom.

rubric.why: An ion has an electrical charge because electrons have been gained or lost.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of an ion.

rubric.why: The presence of an unpaired electron characterises a free radical.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the unpaired electron(s).

rubric.why: A molecule is an independently existing particle made of bonded atoms and retains the substance’s properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of a molecule.

modelAnswer: Atom: The smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction.
Ion: An atom or group of atoms carrying an electrical charge due to the loss or gain of electrons.
Free radical: An atom or group of atoms containing one or more unpaired electrons.
Molecule: The smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retains the chemical properties of that substance.
